_doc: HAND-AUTHORED. Forty cards of EACH volume read, drawn at random and adjudicated one by one against the rendered page image. Nothing else in this domain measures whether the reading is any good; this does, and it is the reason the README can put a number on it instead of an adjective. Schema 2 holds one block per volume, because a number drawn on volume 1 is not a measurement of volume 2 — the top-level counts are the flat total the gate checks, and `volumes` carries the figure that actually belongs to each reading.
generated_by: hand — the draw is reproducible, the verdicts are not

found: One systematic false positive, now struck by a rule: the index carries thousands of English cards citing the Calendarium Inquisitionum by regnal year — 'Calendarium, Hen. III. and Edw. I' — and ', III.' is the shape of ', Ill.'. tools/read_newberry_index.py REGNAL refuses them, and 35 cards left the volume when it was added. The sample was redrawn afterwards and this file adjudicates the redrawn one.
One card this reading should not have kept: nbi_v01_2226, whose whole line is 'I II.'. It is kept, with its verdict, because a struck card nobody can see is a precision figure nobody can check.

Chicago antiquities (Hurlbut, 1881) and the Second Presbyterian Church register 1842-92 (Grant) both surfaced in the sample and neither is in this project's sources. The first is now in the follow-up table.

draw.method: python random.seed(1835); random.sample(chicago_or_cook, 20) + random.sample(the rest, 20), over records/entries_vol_02.json
draw.adjudicated_against: the page image: pdftotext -bbox-layout located each sampled card's own line in its cropped column, and pdftoppm rendered a 212x122-point window around it at 300 dpi, so every verdict below was made looking at the card, its heading and its neighbours

found: THE STATE BANNER ABSORBED AS A CARD BODY — four of the five bad keeps, and a class volume 1's sample did not surface. The index divides a family's cards by state with a printed rule, 'ILLINOIS.'; when that rule falls directly under a heading, the extractor reads it as that card's body and keeps the stanza. nbi_v02_0561, nbi_v02_1675, nbi_v02_1027 and nbi_v02_0539 are the four in this draw, and nbi_v02_1675 is the proof the banner does not belong to the heading above it: the heading is 'Kinge or King family.', whose one card is an English parish register, and the surname run under the banner is KINGERY. All four are kept with their verdicts rather than struck, because a struck card nobody can see is a precision figure nobody can check; T-0600 carries the rule.

A CALL NUMBER READ AS A STATE — the fifth. nbi_v02_1106 is 'Holden family. — Hapgood fam. (Hapgood, W.) 1898. See index. E. 7. H 21', a family genealogy naming no locality; the ', III,' the illinois_abbreviated pattern matched on is the wreck of the Newberry call number. Unlike the banner it names nothing true, and it is the sharper half of T-0600.

THE CHICAGO AND COOK STRATUM IS 20 OF 20 — the cards that set the reading order in follow_up.json did not miss once in this draw, and every bad keep in the volume's sample is in the Illinois-only stratum. Volume 1's single figure of 0.975 could not show this because it did not report by stratum; the blocks here do, and volume 1's rows have been re-counted under the same split without a verdict being changed.

The draw is stratified 20/20 and the volume is not: 501 of the 1,987 kept cards are Chicago or Cook. Weighted by the population the estimate is 0.813, and the unstratified 0.875 above is the figure comparable with volume 1's.

A SLIVER IS A SECOND CARD. nbi_v02_1775 reads 'Krlog | Cook Co..' — the left edge of a card standing in column 3, caught by column 2's 200-point window, which column 3 also read in full as nbi_v02_1779. The passes are deduplicated on (page, heading, body) and a truncated sliver never matches its full sibling. Correct on locality, so it is not counted against precision, and it inflates the card count. T-0601 measures how many.

A CHICAGO CARD LOST TO THE BUCKET. nbi_v02_0937 is 'Henrotin family. — Chicago, Ill. (Andreas, A. T.) 1884-6', and the reading dropped the word 'Chicago' from the body, so it is bucketed illinois_abbreviated and is not among the 501. A recall loss, not a precision error — this sample cannot measure recall, and the 501 is a floor, not a count.

Two works surfaced in the draw that this project already holds and that the follow-up table ranks: the Fergus Historical Series' 1839 Chicago directory (cards under Foster and Graves, both immediately beneath their Andreas card) and the Second Presbyterian Church register 1842-92.

draw.method: python random.seed(1835); random.sample(chicago_or_cook, 20) + random.sample(the rest, 20), over records/entries_vol_03.json
draw.adjudicated_against: the page image: pdftotext -bbox-layout located each sampled card's own line inside its cropped column, and pdftoppm rendered the 200-point column from 52 points above that line to 22 below it at 300 dpi, so every verdict was made looking at the card, its heading, the card above it and any printed banner between them

found: THE COLUMN SLIVER SUPPLIES A LOCALITY THE CARD DOES NOT HAVE — one bad keep (nbi_v03_0913) and, on a card that is otherwise a good keep, one wrong surname (nbi_v03_1154 is filed under the neighbour's 'Onslow'). The crop boxes are 200 points wide on a 173-point pitch, deliberately, so a column always arrives whole; the cost is a sliver of the next column on every page, and where the sliver's first word is 'Illinois' or its heading is nearer the line than the card's own, the assembled card is a hybrid of two columns. Deduplication on (page, heading, body) does not catch it, because the hybrid is not a duplicate of anything. Both are left in the volume, with their verdicts, rather than struck: a card nobody can see is a precision figure nobody can check (volume 1's rule).

'SEE INDEX III.' IS A VOLUME NUMBER — nbi_v03_1443, and it is the class this volume adds. The cards cite a genealogy's index volume in roman, and ', III.' after a stop is the shape the illinois_abbreviated pattern is looking for. It is the regnal problem in a second dress, and it is commoner: two of the four cards in that one rendered window carry the formula.

THE REGNAL RULE PASSES A CARD IT WAS WRITTEN TO STOP — nbi_v03_0653, 'Calendarium, Hen. III. and Edw. I', read by the OCR as 'Calendafium, Han, iii. and i n .'. REGNAL matches the regnal name and a capitalised numeral; here neither survived the photostat. Volume 1 struck 35 cards with that rule and this volume shows what it still lets through.

A PRINTED BANNER IS NOT THE ONLY WAY A NON-ILLINOIS CARD IS KEPT — nbi_v03_1870 is a NEW ENGLAND card whose reading opens 'lil.', which is on no card; the illinois_abbreviated pattern anchors on start-of-line as well as on a comma, and a mark left by the rule above the card satisfies it. Volume 2's banner class and this are the same failure at two different sources.

WIDE PAGES TRUNCATE COLUMN 3's HEADINGS — nbi_v03_0849 is filed under 'rtenoan' because page 375's printed column 3 begins left of the 519-point crop. The card's locality is right and its surname key is not, so it can never join a lead. The crop comment already records that page widths run 689 to 733 points; this is what the widest of them costs.

Nothing in the forty was a Chicago or Cook card that should not have been kept: 20 of 20, as in volumes 1 and 2. Every bad keep in three volumes has been an Illinois-only one, and every one of them has come from text that is not on the card.
